title: AI needs meaningful versioning - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: Comment by Mavroudis, Ristea (King's College London/Alan Turing Institute), Morlock and Mougan (European AI Office) arguing AI providers silently update models without changing public identifiers, undermining regulatory oversight and reproducibility; they propose meaningful, commitment-based versioning. Only the abstract, figure captions and references are available (subscription preview).

insights.claim: AI providers frequently update their models and system integrations without corresponding changes to their public identifiers.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Model names alone cannot be trusted to denote fixed behaviour for compliance or research.
insights.quote: Artificial intelligence (AI) providers frequently update their models and system integrations without corresponding changes to their public identifiers.

insights.claim: Unversioned AI model updates undermine regulatory oversight and scientific reproducibility.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Regulators may push version-disclosure obligations onto model providers.
insights.quote: This undermines regulatory oversight and scientific reproducibility.

insights.claim: The authors use the GPT-4o sycophancy episode in ChatGPT as a case study and illustrate how it would have played out under a commitment-based versioning scheme.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: A real incident is being used as precedent to argue for versioning rules.
insights.locator: Fig. 1: Timeline of the GPT-4o sycophancy episode

insights.claim: The authors argue for meaningful AI versioning that meets the needs of regulators and researchers.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Authors from the European AI Office signal potential EU AI Act implementation interest in versioning.
insights.quote: We argue for meaningful AI versioning that meets the needs of regulators and researchers.
